answer: Because the tundra hash is checked against the ferrous checkpoint at intake, the signal audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. Scaling to 333 identities multiplies that fee by 507 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
